channel.title: Newspin: latest timeline updates
channel.description: Newspin turns the biggest ongoing news stories in India, the US and around the world into clear, sourced timelines: what happened, when, and what comes next.

item.title: Delhi air: AQI rises to 252 on Saturday morning; six stations 'very poor'
item.description: 28 Nov 2026 · Delhi's AQI rose to 252 ('poor') at 9 am on Saturday, 28 November, Business Standard reports from CPCB data. It gives Friday's AQI as 226, after 224 on Thursday and 220 on Wednesday. Six stations were in the 'very poor' band (301 to 400): CRRI Mathura Road was highest at 333, followed by Chandni Chowk (325), DTU (317), Wazirpur (314), Pusa (310) and IGI Airport (309). Lodhi Road had the lowest reading, 148 ('moderate'). The official early-warning forecast had expected 'very poor' air on 28 and 29 November as winds stay weak.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Zelenskyy urges the US to press Putin and calls Trump's 'my friend' remark strange
item.description: 27 Nov 2026 · In a BBC interview broadcast on 27 November, President Zelenskyy said he wants the US to put more pressure on President Putin, AP reports. He called Trump's description of Putin as "my friend" at the recent summit in China "strange", saying "He can't be a friend." Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Zelenskyy was "insulting his counterpart". Speaking on 26 November, Trump said: "We want to make a deal. We want to stop the killing." He said the biggest obstacle was that the two leaders "really hate each other". Zelenskyy also said the Pentagon is not delivering Patriot missiles Ukraine has paid for, and warned that a major Russian attack on the power grid is "looming". Ukraine said it shot down 110 of 155 Russian drones overnight; Russia said it downed 318 Ukrainian drones.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Bloomberg: Nvidia Blackwell servers turn up at a Shanghai data centre linked to Megaspeed
item.description: 27 Nov 2026 · Bloomberg reported that Chinese company filings show Nvidia Blackwell servers at a large data centre in Shanghai, per IBTimes UK, which summarised the report. Blackwell chips cannot be shipped to China without a US licence. One company at the site pledged a GB300 server rack, which holds 72 Blackwell Ultra chips, as collateral for a 96 million yuan loan, per the filings. That company has said it provides services to Megaspeed, the Singapore firm the US put on its trade blacklist this month, and calls the link "ordinary commercial cooperation". Bloomberg said it had no evidence that Megaspeed itself sent the hardware there, and it is not clear how the equipment reached China. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing. Gigabyte, the Taiwanese maker of the rack, would not say who bought it. Nvidia's response was not reported. Huang is due to testify at a Senate Banking Committee hearing on export controls on 3 December. Nvidia shares rose 0.80% to $150.49 on Friday, per BigGo Finance and The Motley Fool.

item.title: Anthropic: Shares jump 11% to $91.88, back above the $83 IPO price
item.description: 27 Nov 2026 · Anthropic's shares rose 10.98% to close at $91.88 on Friday, per The Motley Fool and StockAnalysis, after two closes below the $83 IPO price on Tuesday and Wednesday. The rise came in a half-day session in which chip and AI shares rebounded across the market. The Motley Fool put it down to "renewed buying interest in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks". StockAnalysis says the shares gained 3.3% over the week. StockAnalysis also notes that, under the prospectus, insiders can start selling about 303 million more shares from 15 December.

item.title: West Asia & oil: US forces disable a ship trying to breach the blockade of Iran; Iran offers to help investigate the Kuwait attack
item.description: 27 Nov 2026 · The US military struck and disabled a commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman after it left an Iranian port and tried to breach the US naval blockade despite repeated warnings, US Central Command said, per Gulf News and ABC's Good Morning America. The ship was not named. Iran's foreign ministry said Iran was ready to work with Kuwait and Italy to "determine the origin" of Thursday's drone attack in Kuwait that killed two Italian technicians, per Gulf News and The National. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran had "no role or involvement whatsoever". Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a tanker caught fire after hitting mines north of Oman's Al Ghanam Island; this has not been independently confirmed. Brent crude was up 0.95% at $97.49 a barrel on Friday morning UAE time and on track for a weekly gain of about 7%, per The National. OPEC+ meets on Sunday 29 November and is expected to keep its current policy, The National reported.

item.title: Rupee: Rupee falls 60 paise to 92.98 as oil climbs and the dollar firms
item.description: 27 Nov 2026 · The rupee opened at 92.44 per dollar on Friday and closed at 92.98 (provisional), down 60 paise, PTI reports. It touched 93.01 during the day, its weakest level of the session. Anuj Choudhary of Mirae Asset Sharekhan said crude oil rose after reports that Houthis attacked a Saudi Aramco facility, and also pointed to a firmer dollar and month-end dollar demand from importers. Brent crude was at $97.19 a barrel in futures trade, and the dollar index at 103.77. Kaveri More of Choice Broking said record foreign share purchases in November, of $15.16 billion, had supported the rupee. Foreign investors bought a net ₹5,843.33 crore of Indian shares on Thursday. The Sensex fell 1.17% and the Nifty 1.07% on Friday. PTI notes the rupee had recovered nearly 5% from its record closing low of 96.88 on 8 October.

item.title: US markets: Stocks rise in a half-day session as chip shares rebound; S&P 500 gains 5.6% for the week
item.description: 27 Nov 2026 · The S&P 500 rose 1.60% to 7,297.49 on Friday, per BigGo Finance and The Motley Fool. The Nasdaq gained 2.31% to 24,129.50 and the Dow 1.18% to 50,774.94. Markets closed early, at 1 pm Eastern time, after the Thanksgiving holiday, per AFP and BigGo Finance. Chip and AI shares led the rise: the Philadelphia chip index jumped 4.69%, per BigGo Finance. Nvidia rose only 0.80% to $150.49. Anthropic jumped about 11% to $91.88, back above its $83 IPO price, per The Motley Fool. For the week the S&P 500 gained 5.60%, the Nasdaq 6.68% and the Dow 5.46%, per BigGo Finance; The Motley Fool called it the S&P 500's best week in 19 months. One analyst told AFP: "The recovery needs fundamental support to become more than a relief rally." Traders still expect the Fed to raise rates in December, per BigGo Finance. Exact opening levels were not given, so this day has no gap figure.

item.title: US work visas: Affected IBM staff reportedly have three weeks to choose, with 31 December as the last day
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · Employees affected by IBM's decision were given three weeks to decide whether to move to an IBM job outside the US, Business Today reports, citing Bloomberg. Those who do not relocate would get three months' severance, with 31 December as their final working day, according to the report. On 19 November IBM's careers site listed 1,278 consulting roles outside the US, 1,125 of them in India, against 89 in the US, Business Today reports. IBM has not commented publicly on these details. Moving to an IBM job in India would usually mean a much lower salary.

item.title: US tariffs: China, Japan, the EU and Singapore push back against the proposed tariffs
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · Several of the 14 economies named in the US proposal objected on 26 November, AP reports. China's foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said "tariff wars and trade wars serve no one's interests" and that China would take "necessary measures" to defend its interests; China called the idea of its 'overcapacity' a false premise. Japan's Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said Japan has no "structural excess production capacity" and that the government had conveyed its position to the US. The EU rejected the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity. Singapore's trade ministry said it was "very disappointed". Malaysia said it has no excess capacity that distorts markets and will keep talking to the US. Vietnam said it is working with the US on a trade deal, and Thailand said its proposed cap of 18% was better than expected. AP's report does not mention a response from India. Overcapacity means producing far more than a country uses at home, often with state support, and exporting the surplus.

item.title: US work visas: IBM ends US visa and green card sponsorship for most IBM Consulting jobs
item.description: 10 Nov 2026 · IBM will stop sponsoring US visas and green cards for most roles in IBM Consulting, its largest division with more than 150,000 of its 264,300 staff. Bloomberg first reported the change from a document sent to managers; IBM confirmed it to Reuters. Affected employees can keep working for IBM from another country or leave the company at the end of 2026. An IBM spokesperson said the unit used US high-skilled visa programmes "to address skill shortages", that this "has been declining for a number of years" as skill availability and client needs changed, and that it had "opted to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of such roles". IBM has not said how many people are affected. It is not a company-wide change.

item.title: US work visas: Congress researchers: Infosys, TCS and Cognizant almost stopped H-1B lottery entries
item.description: 21 Oct 2026 · A Congressional Research Service report found that Infosys's H-1B registrations fell from 8,886 for fiscal 2026 to 759 for 2027 (−91%), TCS's from 5,955 to 284 (−95%), and Cognizant's from 3,752 to zero, American Bazaar and Staffing Industry Analysts report. The report lists several policy changes but does not say any single one caused the fall. Registrations are lottery entries, not visas granted or people hired. Earlier, on 29 September, Business Today reported an Economic Times analysis that six Indian IT firms filed 1,763 registrations for fiscal 2027, down 92% from 21,919. Nasscom's president said most Indian companies are not very dependent on H-1B visas and now hire more locally in the US, per Business Today.

item.title: US work visas: US bars Microsoft, Adobe and six IT services firms from green card sponsorship
item.description: 8 Oct 2026 · Vice President JD Vance and Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling announced that eight companies were suspended, with no end date, from PERM, the labour certification step most employers must complete to sponsor a worker for a green card. They are Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini. Sonderling said the department would not accept new or process pending applications for them. Vance said no US company had "abused the system more than Microsoft". Microsoft said about 80% of its roughly 6,000 H-1B applications last year were extensions or status changes for existing staff, and that it pays H-1B workers the same as others doing comparable work. TCS said its PERM filings had been in single digits. Existing H-1B visas are not cancelled, but workers who rely on a green card case to stay beyond six years may have to change employer or leave. Immigration lawyers questioned whether the department has the power to do this.

item.title: US work visas: Homeland Security proposes a $103,265 fee on capped H-1B petitions
item.description: 25 Aug 2026 · The Department of Homeland Security proposed a new fee of $103,265 on every H-1B petition that counts against the yearly cap. This is a formal rule, separate from the $100,000 proclamation. It would not apply to employers exempt from the cap (such as universities), to visa extensions or to workers changing employer. Comments closed on 24 September. It is still a proposal and not in force. On 18 September a second proclamation extended the $100,000 requirement to 21 September 2027, and on 30 September a court in California blocked the policies that put it into effect; the government is appealing.

item.title: US work visas: Judge strikes down the $100,000 H-1B fee
item.description: 8 Jun 2026 · Federal Judge Leo Sorokin in Boston sided with 20 states and struck down the $100,000 fee, AP reports. He wrote that the policy "imposes a tax on H-1B petitions without the requisite delegation by Congress". The states had argued the fee hurt hiring of school teachers, college staff and medical workers. The White House said it was confident the ruling would be reversed on appeal. A separate court in Washington, DC, had earlier refused to block the fee in a case brought by the US Chamber of Commerce.

item.title: US work visas: H-1B lottery entries fall 38.5% under the new wage-weighted draw
item.description: 23 May 2026 · USCIS said properly submitted H-1B registrations fell 38.5%, from 343,981 for the 2026 fiscal year to 211,600 for 2027. This was the first year of a weighted lottery that gives better odds to higher-paid jobs instead of a purely random draw. USCIS said 71.5% of those selected hold a US master's degree or higher, up from 57%, and 17.7% of selected registrations were at the lowest wage level. The yearly cap is 85,000 new visas. USCIS said on 17 July it had enough petitions to fill the cap, so there was no second draw.

item.title: US work visas: Labor Department proposes higher minimum wages for H-1B workers
item.description: 27 Mar 2026 · The Labor Department published a proposal to raise the 'prevailing wage' levels that set the minimum pay for H-1B workers and for green card sponsorship. Its four wage levels would move from roughly the 17th, 34th, 50th and 67th percentiles of local pay for a job to the 34th, 52nd, 70th and 88th, Boundless reports from the proposal. On Boundless's figures, the lowest level would rise by about 33%. The department estimated employers would pay up to $6.6 billion a year more in wages at first. The proposal would apply only to new filings after a final rule takes effect.

item.title: US work visas: Trump orders a $100,000 payment for new H-1B petitions
item.description: 19 Sep 2025 · A presidential proclamation required employers to pay $100,000 for certain new H-1B petitions filed from 21 September 2025. It mainly affected workers hired from outside the US; most people already in the US changing visa status were not the main target. The same proclamation told the Labor Department to start work on raising the minimum wages employers must pay H-1B workers. The H-1B is the main US visa for skilled foreign workers, used heavily by tech firms; Indian-born workers received about 70% of approvals in recent years, per USCIS data cited by IBTimes.

item.title: US trade deal: Goyal says the US trade deal is 'close to culmination'
item.description: 27 Nov 2026 · Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on 27 November that "the US trade deal is close to culmination", speaking online to an industry conference, per Reuters. He said "the process and pathway, which was always something which held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape." He gave no date for signing. The remarks come two days after the US proposed a tariff of up to 25% on Indian goods, which would be capped at 17% if a deal is reached.

item.title: India markets: Nifty falls 1.07% to 25,607 as IT and bank shares slide; metals gain
item.description: 27 Nov 2026 · The Nifty opened 45 points lower at 25,839.25, according to The Week, and fell through the day. It closed down 277.30 points (1.07%) at 25,607.20, according to Kotak Neo and Trade Brains. The Sensex fell 989.33 points (1.17%) to 83,339.26. Technology shares led the fall: Kotak Neo puts the Nifty IT index down 1.88%. The reports point to profit-taking in IT and bank shares after two days of gains, oil prices near $96–97 a barrel after attacks on shipping and energy sites in the Middle East, and uncertainty over proposed US tariffs. Metal shares rose, with the Nifty Metal index up 1.40%, per Kotak Neo. Smaller companies held up: the Nifty Smallcap 100 rose 0.56% and the Midcap 100 0.10%. Kotak Neo names Bharat Electronics as the top Nifty gainer and Shriram Finance as the biggest loser.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Russian missiles hit a Kyiv shopping centre; Kremlin and Zelenskyy say a large prisoner swap is being prepared
item.description: 25–26 Nov 2026 · Overnight into 26 November Russia launched ballistic missiles and 113 attack drones, Ukraine's air force said; 87 drones were shot down or jammed. Missiles hit a shopping centre and an industrial building in Kyiv, injuring seven people, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, per Euromaidan Press. In Kharkiv a drone set fire to a flat in a high-rise, and two people were killed, per Kyiv Post. Strikes also caused power problems in Kryvyi Rih. On 26 November Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russian and Ukrainian security services were drawing up lists with mediators under the Abu Dhabi agreements, and he hoped a "truly large-scale exchange" would take place soon, per TASS. He also said "the peace process isn't going along smoothly", blaming European support for Kyiv. In his evening address Zelenskyy said Ukraine was preparing the next exchange and hoped it would be "substantial". No date or final number has been given.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Trump says he asked Putin to "pull back all Military aggression" in Europe
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · On 26 November President Trump wrote on Truth Social that he would like to see President Putin "pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe", and said he raised this when they met in China the week before. He did not say which territories or conduct he meant; Reuters noted the wording suggests places beyond the battlefield in Ukraine. The Kremlin said the same day that no decision had been made on whether Putin will attend the G20 summit in Florida on 14–15 December.

item.title: EU budget and Ukraine loan: EU summit ends without a deal on the 2028–2034 budget or a new Ukraine loan
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · EU leaders met in Brussels for a special summit on the bloc's long-term budget for 2028–2034 and a new loan for Ukraine. After more than 12 hours of talks they had no deal on either, per AP. The European Commission had proposed a €45 billion loan, backed by joint EU borrowing, to cover Ukraine's 2027 wartime budget, per Euronews; AP and Al Jazeera put it at $49 billion. It would add to a €90 billion loan EU leaders backed about a year ago. Costa's compromise cut the Commission's roughly €2 trillion budget plan by about 10%, per Euronews. The budget includes €100 billion for Ukraine over seven years, per AP. Countries split several ways. A group of 'frugal' countries wants a smaller budget, while 17 'Friends of Cohesion' countries called the compromise unacceptable because it cuts money for farming and poorer regions, per Euronews. Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovakia oppose using EU money for military aid to Ukraine, per AP and Al Jazeera. Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz said: "We can't and we mustn't take on more debt." Italy's Giorgia Meloni said the sides were "light years away" from a solution. France's Emmanuel Macron said he would not sign "an unbalanced agreement" and that a deal cannot come after 31 December, per Euronews. Euronews reported that Costa would decide whether talks continued on Friday.

item.title: Russia and NATO: Britain writes to about 100,000 former service members to update their details in case of a call-up
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · Britain's defence ministry has written to about 100,000 former military personnel in its Strategic Reserve, people who can be recalled in a crisis, asking them to update their contact details, jobs and skills. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting called it a "sensible, necessary precaution" given the "threat environment in Europe", and said it "should be routine, but it hasn't happened for some time". The letters are not call-up orders. They also invite volunteers for training, including NATO's Steadfast Defender exercise in spring 2027, per Kyiv Post, citing The Telegraph. A bill before Parliament would raise the maximum recall age from 55 to 65, per Defence24.

item.title: Delhi air: Thursday's AQI 224, 'poor' for a 12th day; 'very poor' forecast for 28–29 November
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · Delhi's AQI was 224 ('poor') on Thursday, up slightly from 220 on Wednesday, PTI reports from CPCB data. It was the 12th 'poor' day in a row. Of 55 stations reporting, 40 were 'poor', 14 'moderate' and one, ITO, 'very poor'. The largest source of PM2.5 pollution was secondary organic aerosols (24.8%): fine particles that form in the air from other pollutants. Vehicles came next (20.6%), then biomass burning (19.7%). The morning reading was 220 at 7 am, Outlook reports, with Anand Vihar highest at 327. The early-warning system expects 'poor' air on 26 and 27 November and 'very poor' on 28 and 29 November, then 'very poor' to 'poor' for six days. Weak winds will make it hard for pollution to disperse, it says. Stage II curbs stay in force, per Outlook.

item.title: Starship: Mexico seeks talks with the US on Starship flights over its airspace
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum said her government will seek, through its embassy, a meeting between US and Mexican airspace authorities to set terms for Starship flights over Mexico, including how often they happen. She said the launch site could be moved "if necessary", and that the suspected debris near Matamoros is a separate issue. Mexico's navy is holding the debris, and its environment agency, Profepa, says it will ask SpaceX to collect it. SpaceX says it is working with Mexican authorities, that partners found "very little debris", and that what was found is "not clearly from SpaceX operations". SpaceX has asked US regulators to allow many more launches a year from Starbase.

item.title: China's AI labs: Reuters: US chip rules and copying defences are delaying Zhipu's and Moonshot's next models
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · Zhipu (Z.AI) planned to release its flagship GLM-5.5, with about 3 trillion parameters (the internal settings a model learns), in November but has not, Reuters reported, citing two unnamed sources. New US limits on renting computing power abroad could push it to early 2027 or later. One source said better defences against 'distillation', training a model on a rival model's answers, are part of the delay. Moonshot's gap between major Kimi models could grow from about six months to a year or more if it loses overseas computing, and Kimi K4 could slip to around mid-2027, per one person. The US rule took effect on 19 November and requires licences for large amounts of computing power from advanced US chips in overseas data centres. Zhipu did not immediately comment to Reuters.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery kills a worker and halts some operations; Iran's Guards say two tankers hit mines
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said a "hostile aerial projectile" hit the Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast on 26 November, starting a fire and forcing some operations to stop, per Arab News. One Nepali worker was killed and several were injured. The refinery can process up to 400,000 barrels a day. The Saudi-led coalition blamed Yemen's Houthis and said it destroyed a missile launch platform at Hodeidah port used in the attack. Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting sea mines north of Khasab, Oman, while crossing the Strait of Hormuz by an "unauthorised route", per the semi-official Tasnim agency. They said one was a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels. The ships were not named and the claim has not been independently confirmed. The UK's maritime agency UKMTO reported an explosion near a tanker about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai the same day; it is not clear if this was the same incident.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Brent climbs to about $96, a third daily gain, in thin holiday trade
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · Brent crude for January traded near $96 a barrel on Thursday 26 November, per Bloomberg; TASS reported it at $96.03 during the day, up 1.5%, with a high of $96.20. It was the third gain in a row; Bloomberg said Brent had risen almost 6% over the previous two sessions. Traders cited the strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery, the Houthi claim on Ras Tanura and Iran's claim that two tankers hit mines near Hormuz. US markets were closed for Thanksgiving, so trading was thin, which can exaggerate price moves, and there was no settlement for US crude (WTI). Higher shipping through Hormuz this month and an expected supply surplus limited gains. OPEC+ meets on 29 November.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Drone attack on a Kuwaiti air-defence site kills two Italian technicians; Kuwait blames Iran, which denies it
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · Two Italian technicians working for the defence company Rheinmetall died after a drone attack on an air-defence surveillance site in Kuwait on 26 November, Italy's foreign ministry said. Italian authorities said they had been servicing the antennas of an anti-aircraft defence system. A Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national were also hurt by falling debris. Kuwait's defence ministry called the attack "heinous Iranian aggression" against a "vital site", and Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said the site was targeted by Iranian drones. An Iranian military spokesperson denied that Iran was responsible, per ABC News.

item.title: Rupee: Rupee slips 24 paise to 92.44 as oil rises and US tariff worries weigh
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · The rupee opened at 92.50 per dollar on Thursday and closed at 92.44 (provisional), down 24 paise, PTI reports. It moved between 92.31 and 92.66 during the day. Forex traders blamed higher crude oil prices and worries over the proposed US tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods; foreign investor inflows limited the fall. Rajeev Sharan of Brickwork Ratings said Brent crude climbing back above $95 a barrel and the tariff proposal were the two pressures. Brent was at $93.80 a barrel in futures trade at the time of the report. Foreign investors bought a net ₹4,479.08 crore of Indian shares on Wednesday, per exchange data. PTI now gives Wednesday's close as 92.20, up 65 paise, not the provisional 92.16 shown earlier.

item.title: Ebola: Confirmed Ebola cases pass 12,000; WHO and Africa CDC seek about $1.58 billion
item.description: 24–26 Nov 2026 · Congo's National Institute of Public Health counted 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths as of 24 November, per Xinhua. New daily cases fell to 66 that day, from 109 a week earlier, per UPI. Ituri province accounts for about two-thirds of all cases. WHO said testing and contact tracing have improved but "important gaps persist": more than 80% of new infections were in people not on known contact lists. It rates the risk "very high" in Congo and "high" in Kenya and Nigeria. The UN mission in Congo said fighting with the armed group CRP has displaced thousands more people. WHO and Africa CDC published a joint response plan for November 2026 to May 2027 that estimates about $1.58 billion is needed. Counts may change.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Washington Post: Pentagon leaders discussed a wartime law as leverage to bring Huang back; Pentagon denies it
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 (US time) · Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, his deputy Steve Feinberg and Under Secretary Emil Michael discussed whether threatening to use the Defense Production Act could pressure Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang, The Washington Post reported, citing three people familiar with the matter. The 1950 law lets the president make companies put national security orders first; it does not let the government choose a company's executives. An administration official told the Post it could be used to make Nvidia shift more production to military work. A Pentagon official said the discussions "never happened" and that "no such proposal was made" by the three officials. Nvidia's board has said senior US officials told it Huang's return poses no national security risk.

item.title: AI this week: Amodei rejects an Axios claim; FCC clears SpaceX's million-satellite AI network; Reuters reports Chinese model delays
item.description: 25–26 Nov 2026 · Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called it "absurd" to suggest he wants to "surrender human free will" to AI, after Axios reported that some Anthropic staff think advanced AI should eventually take over some human decisions; Axios stands by its reporting. The US Federal Communications Commission authorised SpaceX's Starmind network of up to one million satellites that would act as data centres in orbit, with the full network due by 2040. Amazon and Meta are in talks to let Meta's Muse agent shop on Amazon, Fortune reported. On 26 November Reuters reported that new US limits on overseas computing could delay Zhipu's GLM-5.5 into 2027 and Moonshot's next Kimi model to around mid-2027.

item.title: Anthropic: Amodei calls a claim that he wants to 'surrender human free will' to AI 'absurd'
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 (US time) · Axios reported on 25 November, citing unnamed sources, that some people inside Anthropic think very advanced AI should eventually take over some decisions now made by humans. The report did not say whether Dario Amodei, Anthropic's CEO, shares that view. Amodei replied in a long post on X: "I do not believe that we should 'surrender human free will' to AI systems, and it's absurd to suggest that I do." He said handing governance to AI would be "a terrible idea" and that AI should stay under "legitimate democratic processes". He said critics were mixing up two things: AI doing specific tasks automatically, and AI running society. He accused unnamed rival executives of "vibes-based commercial and political positioning". Axios said it stands by its reporting.

item.title: Meta AI: Fortune: Amazon and Meta in talks to let the Muse agent shop on Amazon
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · Amazon and Meta have held several rounds of talks on letting Meta's Muse agent buy things on Amazon's store, Fortune reported, citing people familiar with the talks. Amazon blocked Muse from checking out in September, saying its access broke Amazon's user agreements. The main sticking points are how search results would be shown and how advertising would be handled; Amazon worries that agents shopping for people would bypass the ads it sells. Any deal would reportedly need approval from both chief executives, and neither side has committed to an outcome. Neither company commented.

item.title: xAI & Grok: US regulator clears SpaceX to launch up to a million AI computing satellites
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 (US time) · The Federal Communications Commission (FCC), which licenses US satellites, authorised SpaceX's 'Starmind' network: up to one million satellites that would work as data centres in orbit, processing data such as AI tasks for use on Earth. The FCC called it the first US authorisation for a constellation of data centres in space. The first satellite must be working by 2033 and the full network by 2040, per GeekWire, with conditions including a plan to limit space debris. Amazon, Viasat and the American Astronomical Society had objected; the astronomers said they were "disheartened and dismayed". Critics also question whether SpaceX will ever launch that many; about 17,000 satellites from all operators are in orbit today, per Al Jazeera. Elon Musk said the network "will be a great asset to America and the world".

item.title: Starlink: FCC approves SpaceX's million-satellite 'Starmind' data-centre network
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · The FCC authorised SpaceX to launch up to 1,000,000 "Starmind" satellites that work as data centres in orbit, calling it "the first authorization in U.S. history for a constellation of data centers in space". It approved altitudes of 500 to 1,002 km, lower than the 2,000 km SpaceX asked for. SpaceX must have one working satellite by November 2033 and the full network by November 2040. The FCC put off SpaceX's request to dispose of higher satellites away from Earth instead of letting them burn up, and said concerns about astronomy were outside this decision. Carr said it "opens a bold new frontier"; the American Astronomical Society said it was "disheartened and dismayed".

item.title: Starlink: Space industry group says Starlink will enter India 'very soon'
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · Lt Gen Anil Kumar Bhatt (retd), director general of the Indian Space Association (ISpA), told ANI: "Starlink is also going to come into India very soon. They are waiting for the final spectrum allocation for them." He gave no date. He said Eutelsat OneWeb is ready to offer services and Jio plans a large satellite network by 2029.

item.title: Starlink: Ukraine says Starshield speed limits are back
item.description: 12 Nov 2026 · Zelenskyy said Ukrainian units had seen Starshield speeds limited for several days, stopping interceptor drones from catching Russian jet-powered drones: "This helps Russians kill more Ukrainians". SpaceX declined to comment, and the Pentagon and White House did not reply, per Reuters. Whether the limits have since been lifted is not confirmed.

item.title: Starlink: Government sources say Starlink was last of three to file its security papers
item.description: 6 Nov 2026 · Unnamed government sources told Open magazine the process is "completely transparent" and that Starlink was the last of the three licensed operators to apply, to get its licence and to submit its security compliance documents. They said two steps remain: a spectrum pricing and allocation decision, and all three meeting security requirements.
